title: clickhouse-format doesn't hilite some identifiers
body:
Hey!

1. In this query the `identifier` is not hilited — is it intended behaviour? I think it should either be hilited as an identifier, or an alias.
```
$ ./clickhouse-format --hilite --query "with identifier as (select * from table) select * from table"
WITH identifier AS
    (
        SELECT *
        FROM table
    )
```
https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Parsers/ASTWithElement.cpp#L21

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5155395/214872393-ab697d98-26a7-45d7-9579-d19071debd43.png)

2. And also there's another identifier output without being hilited, but I cannot come up with the query which corresponds to this code - any help?
https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Parsers/ASTWithAlias.cpp#L23

3. There seems to be an inconsistensy of manually applied hilite, as it's never removed within this if:
https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Parsers/ASTFunction.cpp#L585

comments.body:
Comma prob shouldn't be hilited as a keyword

https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Parsers/ASTTablesInSelectQuery.cpp#L212

What is `JoinKind::Comma`? I couldn't find it in docs, thus couldn't come up with an example query
https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/sql-reference/statements/select/join/


Probably related to this

`clickhouse-format --oneline --hilite --query "SELECT one, two FROM table, mable"`

doesn't hilite the first comma, but does hilite the second one. It's probably an unintentional hilite, as no commas are hilited in ASTExpressionList (first comma).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5155395/228198210-b0358c18-0c52-4405-aee1-a5fe6b2c91a5.png)

I attribute this unintentional behaviour to a dangling `hilite_keyword` in ASTTableJoin:
https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Parsers/ASTTablesInSelectQuery.cpp#L151

The issue is found when testing the https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/45649 refactoring.

**UPD** In this case comma should be hilite as a keyword, as it acts in lieu of JOIN. So no bugs here.
